A task. A keyboard. Proof.

Can I Finish tests whether a keyboard user can complete a real task, and keeps the browser evidence.

REAL WEBSITE / APPLE.COM

Here is a real example on Apple dot com. Find the iPhone VoiceOver setup guide, using only the keyboard.

39 KEY EVENTS / TASK COMPLETED

The runner opens VoiceOver, follows the iPhone setup link, and verifies the destination article. This run passed in thirty nine key events.

INSPECT THE ACTUAL RUN

Every key has a screenshot, a focus record and a timestamp. The report preserves the actual browser recording, and exports a repeatable task contract.

CONTROLLED FIXTURE / BEFORE

Now a deliberately broken registration form. The control responds to a mouse click, but never receives focus during eighteen Tab presses.

SAME CONTRACT / AFTER

Replace that div with a native button, and run the identical contract again. The fixed version reaches registration in five key events.

ESCAPE / EXIT / CONTINUE

A second fixture catches a dialog that ignores Escape. Its fixed version closes, restores focus, and lets the keyboard journey continue.

KEEP THE REGRESSION TEST

Download an executable keyboard regression test and rerun it after a change. The runner is free and local. This is reproducible task evidence, not an accessibility certification.
